issues.cell: the lock sentence's (G2) (adj l. 361-365); E-D6; E-D7; E-V9-5; §7.1's EditFate (base l. 10325); V09's CountBadge.byFate (V09 l. 570); V10's ProposalView.counts.fates

Confirmed fates are stored in each event and compared on replay (base l. 11084-11087): one builder widens the union (V09's record then fails), another stores a reshape as 'kept' with a reason string. E-D7's change list has no value for a fixed place (water gate, anchor) moved with a held stretch, which the fixed-place sentence and E-D3 make.

E-D7's change list adds 'placeMoved' (a fixed place moved with a held stretch by the fixed-place sentence). E-V9-5 adds: V09's CountBadge.byFate -> Record<EditFate['fate'], number>.

issues.cell: W2's, W10's, W13's and W14's last columns (adj l. 690, 698, 701, 702); W2·C8, W13·C8, W14·C8; E-D3 ('each a fate'); (G2) vs the lock sentence's reach; E-D6; §7.3 item 4; §7.1's returned kinds

And a drawn wall (held, locked by default) bent by the bent-group sentence in its author's own moved vertex, re-grade or gate slide is 'reshaped' by E-D6's words (confirm) and takes 'its cell' (the bend) by the reach; W14 names reshaped, W2·C8 and W13·C8 do not, E-S4 decides neither.
issues.required_change: W2's, W10's, W13's and W14's last columns and E-D3: 'each local move a fate' / 'each a fate' -> 'each local move part of the bend, named in its one line (no fate); a vault's removal a fate'. (G2), after 'beside its row's bend line' add: '— never the op's own target: a drawn wall or a declared raised way its author's declaration changes takes its row's bend, no fate, and every other held thing the meeting changes (a locked arch vault, a held raised way's chamber, a held wall the op does not name) the fate reshaped —'. E-D6, after 'takes reshaped' add '(never the target its author's own declaration changes, which the dry run bends)'.

issues.cell: the bent-group list (adj l. 550-555) × beneath's pulled list (adj l. 469-475); W2; E-D3; §7.1 drawWall.from and Points in, shape out (base l. 10341, 10777); bend.wall.ridge (V09 l. 1966); V10's T3 wall encoder (V10 l. 2787)
issues.claim: A drawWall's points form is 'the run derived along ridges and contours by S5a's trace' (base l. 10341, 10777); beneath counts a hand contractWall as pulled because it runs S5a's trace step, while the bent-group list names every hand drawWall. The clerk always sends the points form, the canvas a points form or a drawn line. One builder pulls a points-form stroke across a raised way (widened impassables, the cost path's crossing, a pinless bend through a gate), another lays the S5a line and applies the bent-group sentence ((i)'s nearest lawful crossing and spine-order tie, (ii)-(iii)'s edges): two crossings, and canvas line vs clerk points differ. V06 §3.7.6 (4)'s dossier circuit, 'laid through the hand drawWall operator's path', is pulled: one operator, two laws.
issues.required_change: The bent-group list: 'a hand drawWall (a village T3 wall among them)' -> '... in either form — its points form's run, derived by S5a's trace along ridges and contours (§7.1 Points in, shape out), is laid as that trace derives it and then met by this sentence as a drawn line is, the pull's impassables and pins not read (V06 §3.7.6 (4)'s dossier-admitted circuit, an engine trace, staying beneath's pulled one)'. Beneath's pulled list, after 'a hand contractWall's (§4.11: S5a's trace step)' add '(a drawWall's points form, though derived by S5a's trace, is the bent group's)'. E-S4 adds: a hand drawWall across the standing aqueduct as two points and as a drawn line along the same run — one crossing, the bent-group sentence's, byte-equal through the clerk.

issues.cell: no row: the castle's keep and bailey grips (setAttr(castle,'site'|'baileyArea'), V09 l. 1199-1200; base l. 11472-11473); a terrain stroke on a cliff anchor (§7.4's cliff row, base l. 11444); a warp (base l. 4545-4547, 10452); W2's event cell; E-D3's cause; the fixed-place sentence's and E-D4's 'a drawn castle'
issues.claim: (1) Dragging the castle's keep or bailey re-sites or resizes it: its curtain is its own Enceinte 'bailey' (base l. 2279) and 'S7 re-traces its run when the castle is on the enceinte', moving its weld vertices and town-side gate (fixed places). No row has the event and §7.1 binds no 'drawn castle': builders refuse it (G3), bend it by S3 (8)'s filter, or lay curtain and run by the bent group. (2) A terrain stroke flattening a cliff anchor re-traces a stretch by S7's operator and re-anchors it by F-WALL (base l. 11444) — a hand re-trace W2 does not name. (3) A warp moves an unheld trace with its gates and towers (base l. 4545-4547) under a deck, along beneath it or through a pier; §5.3 holds no raised-way invariant to halve the step against. Builders: the bent group on the warped run, the step halved, or the trace left there.
issues.required_change: W2's event cell adds: '; a castle's curtain and the city run S7 re-traces when its keep or bailey is dragged (setAttr(castle,'site'|'baileyArea'), T3), a stretch a terrain stroke re-anchors (§7.4's cliff row), and a trace a warp moves (§7.1 Warp)'; the bent-group list adds the same three; the fixed-place sentence and E-D4: 'a drawn castle' -> 'a castle sited or resized by hand (setAttr(castle,'site'|'baileyArea'), T3)'; E-D3's cause adds the three ops; E-S4 adds a run for each (the keep dragged so a weld vertex would lie in the declared viaduct's zone — refused refuse.raised.meeting with the nearest clear sites; a cliff stroke beside the aqueduct — the re-anchored stretch by the bent group; a Displace carrying a generated stretch and its gate under the viaduct — the warped run by the bent group, its gate moved clear).

issues.cell: the lock sentence's (G3) (adj l. 365-375) × E-D11's F-WALL raised-way rung (adj l. 1443-1455); W1's hand contractWall (adj l. 689); §5.2's F-WALL stages (base l. 9203); base l. 8662; §7.4's cliff row (base l. 11444); E-S12
issues.claim: (G3) refuses by hand (refuse.raised.meeting) and sends a generation trace to F-WALL. E-D11 heads F-WALL's ladder with a raised-way rung that has no path bound: re-pull once, then 'that stage left unwalled' (W_RAISED_MEETING). F-WALL runs in S3, S5a and S7, and two hand ops run them: a hand contractWall (through S5a's trace step and S7's operator, base l. 8662) and a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor ('re-anchored or walled by F-WALL', base l. 11444). With no lawful meeting one builder refuses the hand op, another re-pulls once and leaves the contraction's ring or the stretch unwalled, reported. E-S12 runs (G3) by hand only for a drawWall and an anchor.
issues.required_change: E-D11's ladder addition: after 'takes its own rung alone, none of the rungs below running on it:' add 'at generation and at a regeneration;' and after '(W_RAISED_MEETING);' add 'on a hand op that runs F-WALL — a hand contractWall (S5a's trace step), a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor (§7.4) — the re-pull is tried once and, where it fails, the dry run is refused (refuse.raised.meeting, §7.1; §2.7's crossing table, (G3)), no stage left unwalled;'. (G3), after 'by hand its dry run is refused' add '(a hand op that runs F-WALL's ladder among them, its raised-way rung's one re-pull tried first)'. E-S12's T110-2 (4) addition adds a hand contractWall across the standing aqueduct on the table-edit variant — re-pulled once, then refused, nothing written.

issues.cell: C13 (adj l. 660-668); A held building in an arch vault's 'no other op moves a span' (adj l. 512-513, PRB7B-05); veto 12; §7.1's binding row for raised ways (base l. 10582); revert / Reset to generated (base l. 11285; V09 l. 3209); the support step (4) (base l. 2551-2552)
issues.claim: C13 names three of the raised way's own ops (a course moveVertex, spanSpacingCm, clearanceCm); §7.1 also binds warp, split, merge, setAttr of class and width, downgradeWay/upgradeWay and revert. A width edit widens the deck's plan, the under-deck strip, the fixed-place zone, held buildings' widened strips and every pier ring ('across the deck of the deck's width'): a band laid after the way that touched a ring at the edge now overlaps it (an aqueduct crossed at a pier), a gate or tower footprint now lies in the strip. A class change between a road class and aqueduct turns a road deck's support the band runs through into an aqueduct's support in a band, or an aqueduct over a standing band into a road deck across a standing trace. A revert of an edited course or spacing moves spans back, so PRB7B-05's 'no other op moves a span' fails and a held building's span can come under a standing wall. No cell; builders bend, refuse or apply.
issues.required_change: C13's event -> 'every op that names it but its decay and repair, a landfall and a frame growth (C3-C6, C10, C12) — a hand re-shape of its course (moveVertex), spanSpacingCm, clearanceCm, its width or class (setAttr, downgradeWay, upgradeWay), a split or merge, a warp that moves its feet or stations, and a revert of any of them'; C13's outcome adds: 'a width or class change re-runs the support step on the whole deck against what stands — a ring that would meet a band laid after the way slid off it by (3), each gate's, tower's and fixed place's footprint and each standing trace's line a wider strip, zone or held building's strip would take in kept out by bending the edit to the nearest lawful width (item 101 R2), and a class change across a standing trace between a road class and aqueduct bent to the class that trace admits — else refused (refuse.raised.meeting)'; A held building: 'and no other op moves a span (...)' -> 'and every other op that would move a span or widen its strip (C13's list, a revert among them) gives way the same; a frame growth's extension keeps the old deck's stations ((7))'. E-S4 adds a width edit and a revert of the re-shape on the held-building fixture.

issues.cell: beneath's vault reading (adj l. 487-506) × a span's use edit; E-V9-8; V09 §4.20.6 (2) (V09 l. 3191-3199); V10's span form and encoder (V10 l. 924, 2810, 2746); §7.1's binding (base l. 10582); §2.7's span record (base l. 2293-2294); V04 l. 370; T-V10-40
issues.claim: On the canvas a span beneath reads open shows 'Walled up as a vault' disabled and sends no event; the clerk's shape { span: { n, use: 'vault' } } encodes setAttr spans/<n>/use with no check, and the base binding applies it (kept open only by a recorded way, water or flood reason), so the record becomes a held vault read open while the wall stands and V04 lays a chamber the user never saw when the wall goes. Builders apply it or bend it as the panel refuses it; canvas and clerk differ, and T-V10-40's byte equality has no canvas event. The path is spans/<ordinal> in §7.1, V09 and V10 but spans/<a>-<b> in §2.7's record and V04: after C13's re-spacing a held vault, and the chamber beneath lays again, land on different spans by form.
issues.required_change: Beneath's vault reading, after 'its record unchanged (the span rule never reads a wall: its step (2), below),' add 'and a user's setAttr of the span's use to vault while beneath reads it open changes nothing, on the canvas and through the clerk alike: the dry run bends it to no change, named in one line with V09 §4.20.6 (2)'s words for what lies under the arch;'. New END under determinism (E-D14): §7.1's binding 'spans/<ordinal>/use' -> 'spans/<a>-<b>/use (the span by its bounding piers' keys, §2.7; a span whose keys an edit re-mints loses its held use, a fate)' and 'kept open over a part-0 way, water or a flood cell by the span's recorded reason' -> '... or while §2.7's crossing table's beneath reads it open'; E-V9-8 adds V09 §4.20.6 (2)'s path -> spans/<a>-<b>/use; under V10, §4.1's span row -> setAttr { id: target, path: 'spans/<a>-<b>/use', value: use }, the n-th span's keys read from the target's card.

issues.cell: W14 (adj l. 702) × the fixed-place sentence (the zone, adj l. 603-605); veto 19; E-S4's W14 runs
issues.claim: The fixed-place zone is the under-deck strip widened by 'the wall strips' widths' — the widths W14 changes (a palisade re-kinded inner, a light stretch re-graded full). W14 keeps the trace and moves only crossings, towers and gates; fixed places 'never move along the trace' and only 'a trace laid after the raised way moves the place itself'. A standing water gate outside a viaduct's zone read with a palisade's strips lies inside it once they widen. Builders leave it (E-S3's 0-in-zone bar fails), re-trace the run to move the crossing (against the kept trace), refuse the re-section, or read the zone with the old widths. The zone names no wall: two rings of different classes give two widths.
issues.required_change: W14·C2 adds: '; a fixed place of the run that its new widths would bring into a standing raised way's fixed-place zone (the zone read with those widths) moves as a trace laid after the raised way moves it — its river crossing along the river, its anchor with its tower along its barrier's edge, the run re-traced locally to it by the bent-group sentence — and a castle's weld vertex or town-side gate it would bring in takes (G3) (by hand refuse.raised.meeting; at a village epoch waiting)'; the fixed-place sentence: 'widened each side by the wall strips' widths' -> '... widths of the wall whose fixed place it is tested against, at that place (§4.8's rows along its stretch profile)'. E-S4 adds the hand drawWall's river stretch re-kinded wider beside the declared viaduct — its water gate moved along the river clear of the new zone, a fate.

issues.cell: the lock sentence's retaining-wall clause (adj l. 376-391); veto 20; E-S9
issues.claim: 'A retaining wall has no band, strip, gate, tower or closure', but RetainingWall carries decorative towers and buttresses (base l. 2323; drawn from the retaining rows, base l. 6982; V11 row 79; set by setAttr, base l. 10589): across a raised way a tower may stand in the under-deck strip above a soffit (the cap reads an enceinte's run only) or a buttress where a support stands — kept out, capped or left, by builder. And the clause's rules (no levelling in the strip; giving way to a held building) bind 'a retaining wall drawn' (T3 retaining, a T2 terrace stroke); a chain point dragged by its grip (V09 l. 1207) or a terrace level re-expansion (V09 l. 1208) across a span seating a held building is moved off, or the chamber removed and the building unseated.
issues.required_change: The clause: 'A retaining wall has no band, strip, gate, tower or closure, so no row of this table reads it' -> 'A retaining wall has no band, strip, gate or closure, so no row of this table reads it; its decorative towers and buttresses (§2.7 RetainingWall; V11 §3.24.1) stand nowhere in an under-deck strip — one its row would place there moved along its line to the nearest point clear of it (Strips, zones and nearest points), by hand a fate in §7.1's catch-all line —'; and 'a retaining wall drawn across a standing raised way (T3 retaining, a T2 terrace stroke)' -> 'a retaining wall drawn or moved across a standing raised way (T3 retaining, a T2 terrace stroke, its chain grip's moveVertex, a terrace level's re-expansion)'. E-S9 adds the stroke with towers on (none in the strip) and a drawn retaining wall's chain point dragged across the held building's span (moved as the drawn stroke is).

issues.cell: W1·C8 '(nothing is held at a first generation)' (adj l. 689); C8's description; the table's 'whichever was laid first' (adj l. 329); §7.2 Declared means held and Drawn constraints (base l. 10816-10832); §4.1's read-ahead (base l. 5121-5135); Points in, shape out (base l. 10767); T101-4, T101-6 (base l. 18439-18445)
issues.claim: A skeleton's declarations are held (base l. 10816-10817) and enter as the creation prefix in resolved form; 'S3 takes the declared walls ... as the enceinte's pinned trace ...; S4 and S5b take the declared roads (drawWay) as fixed routes' — the form Rebuild around my drawings gives too. So held walls and raised ways stand at a first generation and meet in stage order, S3's wall before S4's raised road, where the hand map met them in log order (a raised road declared, a wall drawn beneath it: W2·C2). Read ahead, a road deck 'never crosses a trace standing when its course is laid', yet its course is stored and 'no ... later derivation re-derives or moves an accepted shape'. Builders keep the log's meeting, bring the held deck down, drop it, or re-place its supports; an aqueduct declared before a drawn wall gains slid supports. T101-4's round-trip digest and T101-6's three authorings pass in one build only; W1·C8 denies the case, so no cell or test holds it.
issues.required_change: W1·C8 -> 'as W1·C2, by the lock sentence; the held walls and raised ways of a creation prefix (a skeleton's, §4.1; and those Rebuild around my drawings moves into the recipe, §7.2) meet each other in the prefix's log order, each meeting as its declaration's dry run resolved and stored it (the later one's cell, never re-met in stage order), and every generated structure meets them as held ones standing before its stage · T101-4, T101-6'; the table's lead, after 'whichever was laid first' add '(of two declarations in a creation prefix, the one earlier in the log)'. New END under scope (E-S13): T101-4 adds skeletons exported from a hand map with a raised road declared and a wall drawn beneath it, and from one with the wall first and the road down before it, each re-imported to its source's model digest.

issues.cell: A held building in an arch vault's refuse.locked (adj l. 506-524); the retaining-wall clause (adj l. 388-389); C13 (adj l. 666-667); §7.1's lock row and returned kinds (base l. 10631, 10678-10682); V09's refuse.locked row (V09 l. 1983); V10's lock category (V10 l. 2411); T-V9-13 with E-V9-7 (V09 l. 4372)
issues.claim: The held building is a declared placement (T6 place in the chamber, a skeleton placeAt; V04 l. 1722-1723), held by its declaring event's pin (base l. 10804-10805, 10811), not a T10 lock. The family's three refusals naming it go through §7.1's lock row, whose returned kind is unlock with the building as target; V09 words it '{thing} is locked. Unlock it to change it' with button.unlock, and the clerk offers Unlock. Unlocking a pinned building changes nothing, so the button's preview refuses again, against T-V9-13's 'each button yields a preview that is ok or a new bend'. Builders: the dead Unlock, an unpin the returned kinds lack, or no release.
issues.required_change: A held building in an arch vault, the retaining-wall clause and C13, at each '(refuse.locked, ... the blocking entity)' add: '— its offered actions the closest acceptable declarations and Show me why alone, the building held by its placement, never by a lock to undo (no unlock)'. New END under determinism (E-D13): §7.1's returned kinds, unlock's '— its target the blocking entity' -> '— its target the blocking entity where that entity is locked; a blocker held by a declaration or pin alone (a held building in an arch vault, §2.7's crossing table) returns no unlock'. New END under V09 (E-V9-9): refuse.locked's second form '{thing} stands where you placed it; choose one of the marked places.', buttons button.chooseMarked and button.showWhy.

issues.cell: down before the wall by hand (adj l. 450-455) × E-D1 (adj l. 1369-1380); veto 10; the lock sentence's list of changes (adj l. 339-343)
issues.claim: By hand a raised road comes down before the trace, its ground way gated there (in a held wall reshaped), 'and the stroke's course beyond the trace carried on as that ground way on ground part 0 to the stroke's end'. E-D1 exempts from §7.1's lock row only 'a raised road's ground way making its gate by hand in a held wall it comes down before'. A stroke across an outer and an inner ring runs on as a ground way across the inner; where that ring is held (drawn, so locked by default, or T10-locked) the crossing is 'a drawn way across a locked entity' — refused by E-D1 read a contrario — while the lock sentence's list and veto 10 make a gate there, reshaped. Builders: the stroke refused, cut before the second ring, or gated twice.
issues.required_change: Down before the wall by hand, after 'a second raised way only by a second declaration' add: '— that ground way crossing every later trace on its course as it crosses the first, at a gate §7.3's S7 operator makes there, in a held wall too, the fate reshaped'; E-D1: 'a raised road's ground way making its gate by hand in a held wall it comes down before among them' -> 'a raised road's ground way making its gates by hand in every held wall it crosses, from the one it comes down before to the stroke's end, among them'. E-S2 adds the hand raised road across the drawn ring and on across a second ring drawn inside it — a gate made in each, each reshaped.

issues.claim: C10 refuses 'a part (3) and (4) cannot place within their bounds' with refuse.raised.meeting — (3)'s obstacles being any way, water, square, reservation or band — while E-D4's cause is a part 'whose supports cannot leave a standing band'. issues.cell: §7.4 Every kind at the edit boundary (base l. 11438-11452) and its B-EDIT test (base l. 11454-11457); E-D10

The retaining-wall row's lock cell reads 'a locked wall masks the stroke on its high side', though the lock sentence makes a retaining wall a similar structure meeting a raised way with its placement held; no row is an enceinte's or an arch vault's, whose locks the lock sentence changes most, so B-EDIT's 'the named outcome at each meeting' names none for them. §2.7 decides the outcomes.
issues.required_change: E-D10 adds: the retaining-wall row's lock cell -> '... on its high side; with a raised way its placement held, its line met by §2.7's crossing table (its lock sentence)'; and rows '| an enceinte (its stretches, gates and towers) | §7.1's T3 rows | its placement held, its shape where a raised way meets it §2.7's crossing table's (its lock sentence) | the event's inverse | a held one stands before every stage |' and '| an arch vault | a span's use; V04's reconcile | its span and key held, its chamber not laid while §2.7's crossing table's beneath reads the span open (its lock sentence) | the event's inverse, its id kept by its key | V04 lays it by the span rule |'.
